references.text: Concerns compensation for damage inflicted on another person, within the same legal context of personal injury and restitution
The continuation of the law describing the consequences if serious harm occurs - the lex talionis principle
Addresses compensation and fines in connection with harm to human life
Similar structure with fines that are determined and paid to the injured party
Law regarding intervention in a fight between men and subsequent punishment
Fundamental principle of human life and its sanctity underlying this law
Describes God's care for the human being in the mother's womb, relevant for understanding the value of the unborn child
Both verses in the same legal code illustrate contrasting principles of liability for harm: human negligence requires compensation, while an animal's violence does not burden the owner with guilt.
